memoryText: For the word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 1 Corinthians 1:18 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Paul writes this verse to a church that was dazzled by wisdom and rhetoric.

“The word of the cross.” The gospel is a message about a crucifixion. In the ancient world, crucifixion was the most shameful death, reserved for slaves and rebels. To say that God’s salvation came through a crucified man sounded insane.

“Is folly to those who are perishing.” To those who are on the way to destruction, the message looks like nonsense. This is not because the message is irrational, but because sin has darkened understanding. Without the Spirit, no one sees its glory.

“But to us who are being saved.” The present tense describes an ongoing process: we are being saved, as the Spirit applies the gospel to our lives. The verse divides humanity into two groups, and the dividing line is the cross.

“It is the power of God.” What looks like weakness is strength. The cross is not just the means of forgiveness but the power that changes lives, raises the dead, and breaks the grip of sin.

If you are ever embarrassed by the gospel, say this verse. The message you carry is the power of God.
weekInReview: This week you finished Galatians and began 1 Corinthians. Galatians 5 and 6 showed how freedom in Christ works: through love, by walking in the Spirit, producing the fruit of the Spirit, bearing one another’s burdens, and boasting in nothing but the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. First Corinthians opened with a divided, gifted church, and Paul answered every division with the word of the cross, the power and wisdom of God. You studied the church as God’s field, building, and temple, with ministers as servants and stewards. Two psalms taught trust: Psalm 33, the counsel of the LORD stands forever, and Psalm 62, for God alone my soul waits in silence. In chapters 5 to 7, Paul dealt with sexual sin, lawsuits, and marriage, always grounding his commands in the gospel: you were washed, sanctified, and justified, and you were bought with a price.
reflectionQuestions: Paul says the message of the cross seems foolish to the world. Where do you feel pressure to make the gospel more impressive or more respectable? What would it look like to trust the cross itself?

First Corinthians 6:11 says “such were some of you” but you were washed, sanctified, and justified. How does this verse change the way you see your past, and the way you see those who are far from God?
Psalm 62 says “For God alone my soul waits in silence.” What is one thing you tend to rely on besides God alone? What would it look like to wait on him this week?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that the word of the cross is the power of God.
Thank him that you are being saved.
Rest in what he has done.
